findings.title: Bacteria are found down to 40 read pairs in 4M, but the species label is often wrong or missing
findings.what: Ten isolates' real reads were mixed into 4,000,000 real human read pairs at 1e-2 to 1e-5. Kraken2 (16 GB, confidence 0.0) called all 8 bacteria at 1e-2, 1e-3 and 1e-4 with 10 or more read pairs, and 6 of 8 at 1e-5 (40 pairs). With confidence 0.1 detection falls: 7 of 8 at 1e-4 with 1 or more pairs, only 3 of 8 at 10 or more; at 1e-5 only 1 of 8.
findings.caveat: Reads come from clean isolates, so real samples with kit contamination and a more varied background will do worse. One run per level, no replicates.

findings.title: Most spiked reads do not land on the species
findings.what: Median species-level recovery of spiked pairs was about 20% at confidence 0.0 and 2% at 0.1. Example: E. coli isolate reads mostly stop at the family Enterobacteriaceae (198,238 of 300,000 pairs) because many Escherichia, Shigella and Salmonella genomes share k-mers. So a species count is a poor measure of load, and a genus or family count may be the honest unit.
findings.caveat: Specific to Kraken2 with the 16 GB capped standard database; not tested with Bracken or a larger database in Phase 2.

findings.title: Both yeasts were invisible to Kraken2
findings.what: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Cryptococcus neoformans got 0 read pairs at every level, even at 40,000 pairs (1%). The standard database has no fungal genomes. MetaPhlAn 4 saw one of the two yeasts at 1e-2 and 1e-3.
findings.caveat: A database choice, not a property of the algorithm. A fungal database would be needed; not run here.

findings.title: MetaPhlAn 4 loses the rare end first
findings.what: MetaPhlAn 4 found 8 of 8 bacteria at 1e-2 and 1e-3, 2 of 8 at 1e-4 and 0 of 8 at 1e-5. It reports a relative abundance for species with marker genes, so it is built for communities, not for a 0.001% pathogen in blood.
findings.caveat: Different question from Kraken2: marker genes, no read counts.

findings.title: False alarms: zero on human-only at 10 pairs, but noise rises with the microbe load
findings.what: The human-only control (spike_H0) had 0 false species at 10 or more pairs in both settings, and 2 false species of pathogen genera at 3 pairs (Mycobacterium, confidence 0.0). In the spiked panels at confidence 0.0, 6 to 16 wrong species passed 10 pairs, mostly near relatives of the spiked organism (Listeria, Bacillus, Burkholderia, Actinomyces). Confidence 0.1 cut that to 0 or 1.
findings.caveat: The human-only floor does not carry over to samples with real contaminants. Near-relative calls look like a species-naming problem, not a new organism.

findings.title: Real plasma runs: the species list is mostly skin, kit and viral commensals
findings.what: 16 Uganda sepsis plasma runs (500,000 pairs each, human rRNA depleted): 1 to 32% human by Kraken2, 58 to 90% unclassified. Species with 10 or more pairs per run ranged 0 to 10. The most common calls were Cutibacterium acnes (12 of 16 runs), E. coli (8), Acidovorax (5), Ralstonia and Brevundimonas, plus torque teno virus and pegivirus. Where a species was called, a large share of reads was in known reagent-contaminant genera (up to 74%).
findings.caveat: No per-sample truth exists in the open data (qPCR results are not public), so this shows behaviour, not accuracy. Cutibacterium, Escherichia and Ralstonia can be contaminants or real infections; the data cannot tell.

findings.title: Kraken2 and MetaPhlAn almost never agree on plasma
findings.what: On the first 6 plasma runs the two tools shared at most 1 species (Jaccard 0.0 to 0.1). MetaPhlAn called almost nothing, Kraken2 called up to 10.
findings.caveat: Six runs only. Disagreement flags where a human should look; it does not say which tool is right.
